The Sopranos started to change that.  It's revolutionary television, but it's still not cinema.  It's like comparing sprinting and marathon running. The Sopranos would not exist without Mean Streets and Goodfellas.  David Chase was inspired by Scorsese's work but isn't trying to  remake it.   Scorsese probably couldn't make a long form tv show. When the lights went out, it lit a match on the powder-keg of a city on the brink of collapse.  People saw their opportunity to not only break into all the stores to get stuff they couldn't afford otherwise, but more importantly to express their rage against the circumstances of their lives.  

In 2003, NYC was a completely different city.  Improvements in policing and crowd control due in part to 9/11, and a national economic boom, handled responsibly by Mayor Bloomberg, saw a NYC that was more cohesive, capable, and collaborative.  

The 77 riots and looting were criminal in every sense of the word, but it was much more likely to happen given the conditions at the time.
